Page Summary outlined_flag When calling the Google Ads API, you need both OAuth 2.0 application credentials and a developer token. If making API calls with a Google Ads manager account, you must specify a login-customer-id header. You can use desktop/web app flows or service accounts to obtain OAuth 2.0 credentials. A developer token is required in the developer-token HTTP header for every API call. The request-id response header uniquely identifies an API request and is useful for debugging. Note: If you are new to the Google Ads API, we recommend reading the Getting
Started guide first, which covers how to
set up your account and make your first API call. Make sure to follow the curl tab. You need OAuth 2.0 credentials when calling the Google Ads API. If you're making API
calls with a Google Ads manager account, you also need to specify a login-customer-id header with each request. This page describes how to set
these values and documents several additional API-specific HTTP headers that are
sent and received when using the REST interface. OAuth 2.0 credentials The Google Ads API uses OAuth 2.0 for authorizing API requests. Both OAuth 2.0 user
authentication flow and service
account flow are supported. For more details,
see OAuth 2.0 in the Google Ads API . If you are new to Google APIs, you can use the gcloud command-line
tool or the OAuth 2.0
Playground to experiment with OAuth
2.0 credentials and the Google Ads API before writing code for your app. We recommend that you use one of the OAuth 2.0 libraries available at https://oauth.net/code/ to implement the OAuth 2.0
authorization workflows. However, we have listed the curl instructions in case
you need to implement it yourself. Service accounts Follow the steps to configure a Google Cloud project for the
Google Ads API . Record the service account email and service account key . Next, follow the
common instructions in the Service
Accounts guide to set
up the service account to access your Google Ads account. User authentication Follow the steps to configure a Google Cloud Console project for the
Google Ads API . Record
the client ID and client secret . Next, follow the desktop app flow
instructions or the web app flow
instructions to generate a refresh token and an access token . The scope to use
for Google Ads API access is https://www.googleapis.com/auth/adwords . Generate new access tokens Service accounts When you have the service account email and service account key ,
follow the Using OAuth 2.0 for Server to Server Applications guide to generate a JWT claim set , which can then be exchanged to obtain
an OAuth 2.0 access token. Make sure to select the HTTP/REST tab while
following the guide. The OAuth 2.0 scope to use for Google Ads API access is https://www.googleapis.com/auth/adwords . In addition, you can skip the sub parameter when constructing the JWT claim set, because the setup steps
grant the service account direct access to the Google Ads account, thus avoiding
the need to impersonate a Google Ads user. You then use the access token in the Authorization HTTP header of
every API call to the Google Ads API: GET /v26/customers:listAccessibleCustomers HTTP/1.1
Host: googleads.googleapis.com Authorization: Bearer ACCESS_TOKEN User authentication Once you have an OAuth 2.0 client ID , client secret , and refresh
token , you can generate a new access token for use in API calls with the curl command line tool: Note: The version v3 in the OAuth endpoint URL is unrelated to the Google Ads API
version and shouldn't change when migrating to newer versions of Google Ads API. curl \ --data "grant_type=refresh_token" \ --data "client_id= CLIENT_ID " \ --data "client_secret= CLIENT_SECRET " \ --data "refresh_token= REFRESH_TOKEN " \ https://www.googleapis.com/oauth2/v3/token You then use the access token returned by the curl request in the Authorization HTTP header of every API call to the Google Ads API: GET /v26/customers:listAccessibleCustomers HTTP/1.1
Host: googleads.googleapis.com Authorization: Bearer ACCESS_TOKEN Request headers The following sections describe the HTTP headers required or used when making
requests to the Google Ads API. Login customer ID For Google Ads API calls made by a manager to a client account (that is, when logging
in as a manager to make API calls to one of its client accounts), you also need
to supply the login-customer-id HTTP header. This value represents the Google Ads
customer ID of the manager making the API call. Including this header is equivalent to choosing an account in the Google Ads UI
after signing in or clicking your profile image at the top right corner of the
page. When specifying the customer ID, be sure to remove any hyphens (—). For
example: 1234567890 , not 123-456-7890 . Refer to the Google Ads access model
guide to learn more about login customer ID. GET /v26/customers:listAccessibleCustomers HTTP/1.1
Host: googleads.googleapis.com
Authorization: Bearer ACCESS_TOKEN login-customer-id: MANAGER_CUSTOMER_ID Key Point: If you're not authorizing as a manager account--in other words, if
your OAuth 2.0 credentials are for a user of the target Google Ads client account
directly--you don't need to supply a login-customer-id header. Linked customer ID The Linked customer ID header is used by partners (such as third-party app
analytics providers or data partners) when acting on a linked Google Ads account.
See the API Call Structure
guide for more details. Authorization: Bearer ACCESS_TOKEN login-customer-id: PARTNER_CUSTOMER_ID linked-customer-id: ADVERTISER_CUSTOMER_ID Response headers The following headers are returned in HTTP responses from the API. Request ID The request-id is a string that uniquely identifies the API request. When
debugging or troubleshooting problems with specific API calls, the request-id is an important identifier to have handy when contacting Google developer
support. Tip: To view response headers, including google-ads-request-id , when using
curl, add the -i or --include option to your command. request-id: 2a5Cj89VV7CNhya1DZjjrC Previous arrow_back Overview Next REST interface design arrow_forward Send feedback Except as otherwise noted, the content of this page is licensed under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 License , and code samples are licensed under the Apache 2.0 License . Page Summary outlined_flag Google Ads API developer tokens have an access level determining production account access and operation limits, and "permissible use" defining allowed API features. There are three access levels: Test Account Access for test accounts with a 15,000 operation limit, Basic Access for test and production accounts with a 15,000 operation limit, and Standard Access for test and production accounts with an unlimited operation limit. You start with Test Account Access and can apply to increase your access level through additional steps. Permissible use, applicable to Basic and Standard Access, is based on intended API use and determines specific feature access like ad creation/management, reporting, or keyword research. Your Google Cloud project is assigned an access level and "permissible use." The access level determines whether you can affect production accounts and the
number of operations and requests that you can execute daily. Permissible
use determines the specific Google Ads API features that the project is allowed to
use. Key Point: Getting started with the Google Ads API? Developer tokens were sunset on September 9, 2026 , and API access levels are now managed
per Google Cloud project. After you enable the Google Ads API (which grants Test access), you can immediately apply on
the Google Ads API Overview page in the Google Cloud Console for Explorer access (automated review and approval in
most cases, for up to 2,880 operations per day against production accounts). For
end-to-end setup, see the Make your first call quickstart or
the Google Ads MCP server guide . Go to Google Ads API Overview in
   Cloud Console Access levels There are four different API access levels listed in order in the
table. If you don't already have Google Ads API access, you can start by enabling the API to obtain Test access
level for your Google Cloud project, and then apply for Explorer
access on the Google Ads API Overview page to access
production accounts. Access level Can access... Daily operation limit 1 How to apply How long do reviews typically take? Test Test accounts 15,000 operations / day Apply for Test access Explorer Test and production accounts 2,880 operations / day for production accounts 15,000 operations / day for test accounts Apply for Explorer access Basic Test and production accounts 15,000 operations / day for both test and production accounts Apply for Basic access Standard Test and production accounts Unlimited operations / day for both test and production accounts Apply for Standard access 10 business days 1 "Per day" is based on a sliding 24 hour time period in which API
requests were made with your Google Cloud project. Your application will receive
an error if it exceeds the request limit for your access level within the last
24 hours. Test access After you've enabled Google Ads API, your Google Cloud project is granted Test access.
This means that the project can only make Google Ads API requests against test
accounts. Important: Refer to the test account guide to learn more about
how to create a test account. Apply for Test access Enable Google Ads API in your Google Cloud project to automatically be granted Test access for your
project. Explorer access level After you've completed the initial sign-up for the Google Ads API, Google may let you
apply for Explorer access level. The Explorer access level allows your Google Cloud project to make Google Ads API
requests against both test accounts and production accounts. Production
accounts are any accounts that serve real, live Google ads—test accounts
don't serve ads. The Explorer access level allows your Google Cloud project to execute up to
2,880 operations per day against production accounts. This is sufficient for
most developers to get started with the API and build basic automation. The Explorer access level restricts access to the following features. If you
need to use these features, you need to apply for Basic access level or Standard access level . Restricted functionality Restricted services and methods Account creation and linking CustomerService.CreateCustomerClient CustomerClientLinkService CustomerManagerLinkService User management CustomerUserAccessInvitationService CustomerUserAccessService Planning KeywordPlanService KeywordPlanIdeaService KeywordPlanCampaignService KeywordPlanCampaignKeywordService KeywordPlanAdGroupService KeywordPlanAdGroupKeywordService AudienceInsightsService ReachPlanService Account billing and payment PaymentsAccountService BillingSetupService AccountBudgetProposalService InvoiceService Multi-party approvals MultiPartyAuthReviewService Apply for Explorer access level Navigate to the Google Ads API Overview page in your Google Cloud
project. Verify that the page displays your current access level as Test . Click to expand the Upgrade access level section. Confirm that the Next access level is displayed as Explorer . Click the Apply for access button to apply for Explorer access level. Google may automatically upgrade your project's API access level to Explorer
after you submit your application. Basic access level The Basic access level allows your Google Cloud project to make Google Ads API requests
against both test accounts and production accounts. Production accounts are
any accounts that serve real, live Google ads—test accounts don't serve
ads. The Basic access level allows your Google Cloud project to execute up to 15,000
operations per day. This is sufficient for most developers. Apply for Basic access level Note: Completing brand verification for your Google Cloud project is a
prerequisite to apply for Basic access level. Refer to the brand verification
guide to learn more. Navigate to the Google Ads API Overview page in your Google Cloud
project. Verify that the page displays your current access level as Explorer . Click to expand the Upgrade access level section. Confirm that the Next access level is displayed as Basic . Confirm that there are no warnings indicating that you haven't completed
brand verification for your project. If there are, follow the instructions to complete brand verification
before continuing. Click the Apply for access button to apply for Basic access level. Google may automatically upgrade your project's API access level to Basic
 once you submit your application. Standard access level Standard access level allows your Google Cloud project to execute an unlimited
number of operations per day for all services. Individual services and features
may still have rate limits and restrictions that are specific to
those features, which will continue to apply even if your project has Standard
access level. The Standard access level is only granted to developers who require unlimited
Google Ads API operations, such as large companies or tools that serve many users. Apply for Standard access level Navigate to the Google Ads API Overview page in your Google Cloud
project. Verify that the page displays your current access level as Basic . Click to expand the Upgrade access level section. Confirm that the Next access level is displayed as Standard . Click the Start application button to start the Standard access level
application. The Standard access application involves a detailed manual audit of your
application. Be prepared to answer questions about your tool's functionality and
its target audience. If your tool is used by external users, be prepared to
provide demo sign-in access to your tool. Note that your tool must comply with
the Required Minimum Functionality . Throughout the review process, the Google Compliance team will communicate with
you using your email address. Make sure you respond promptly to the queries from
the Compliance team to make progress with your Standard access application. When
the review is complete, Google will email you with the final outcome of the
review process. API quotas and system rate limits Regardless of the access level, all API operations are subject to system rate
limits, which restricts how many operations you may perform in a period of time,
that is the number of operations per hour. To learn more about how to handle
rate limit errors, see error types . Individual services may enforce additional limits and quota restrictions due to
reasons such as product design limitations, product policy restrictions, API
performance and latency considerations. See the documentation about API
quotas to learn more about these restrictions. Permissible use Permissible use only applies to Google Cloud projects with Standard access
level. Permissible use is allocated based on intended use of the Google Ads API. These
permissions determine which features of the API your tool can use, as
elaborated in the following table: Permissible Use Description Ad creation / management Provide access to all services of the API for creating and managing Google Ads campaigns, ad groups, ads, and keywords. Reporting Only make GoogleAdsService.Search or GoogleAdsService.SearchStream requests, or read-only calls. This is for developers who only use the API to request stats. Researching keywords and recommendations Allow the Google Cloud project to access RecommendationService , KeywordPlanIdeaService , and KeywordPlanService . This is only used by tools requiring suggestions to help facilitate the creation and management of Google Ads campaigns. Change permissible use If your Google Cloud project has been approved for Standard access level, you
can fill out the application to update permissible use . Fill out
the application if you would like to update your permissible use or grant your

The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open standard that lets large
language models (LLMs) securely interact with external data and applications.
The Google Ads MCP server provides a standardized bridge to the Google Ads API. It lets
AI agents retrieve and analyze account data, create assets, upload videos, and
manage labels by using natural language. Community resources and support GitHub repository: Find demos and examples, report bugs, or suggest
features in the google-ads-mcp repository . Use the Issues tab for bug reports and feature requests. Community: Join the #ads-api-ai-tools channel on the Google
Advertising Community Discord . Technical overview Integrating the Google Ads MCP server removes the need to write custom code for
Google Ads API authentication, resource fetching, data parsing, and supported asset or
label mutations. The server exposes callable tools and reference resources (see Core capabilities ) that an LLM
can inspect and invoke. Key specifications Protocol: MCP (Model Context Protocol) Mode: Read and partial mutate (asset creation, video uploads, and label
management with propose-and-confirm validation , or configurable read-only mode ) Language: Python 3.10 or later Transport: Standard input/output ( stdio ) or Streamable HTTP
( streamable-http on Cloud Run) Authentication: Application Default Credentials (OAuth 2.0 user
credentials or service account) for local stdio , or OAuth 2.0 Web
application credentials for remote HTTP Telemetry: Appends google-ads-mcp/VERSION to the x-goog-api-client gRPC request header for usage statistics How the interaction loop works Request: You submit a prompt such as "How is my campaign performance
this week?" or "Create a callout asset for our summer sale" . Discovery: The LLM inspects its available tools and resources and
selects a matching google-ads-mcp tool. Execution or dry-run validation: Read tools query the Google Ads API directly.
Mutate tools first run in propose mode ( validate_only=True ) to validate
inputs without committing changes (see Propose-and-confirm safety
workflow ). Context injection: The MCP server returns structured query results, or
proposed change_items entries and a verification checksum digest, to the
LLM's context window. Response and confirmation: The LLM presents an answer or asks you to
confirm the proposed changes. After you approve, the LLM calls the mutate
tool again with validate_only=False and the matching checksum value to
commit the change. Get started Follow these steps to configure and run the Google Ads MCP server locally. To deploy
a shared remote service instead, see Deployment on Google
Cloud . Prerequisites Before you configure the server, complete the following prerequisites in your
local environment and the Google Cloud console : Google Cloud project: Create or select a Google Cloud project with the
Google Ads API enabled. Enabling the API grants Test access for testing read
and mutate workflows against test accounts . To access
production accounts, check the Google Ads API overview page for
Explorer, Basic, or Standard access, or apply for one of these access
levels . Otherwise, production calls fail with an AuthorizationError.CLOUD_PROJECT_NOT_APPROVED_FOR_PRODUCTION error. Google
sunset developer tokens ( GOOGLE_ADS_DEVELOPER_TOKEN ) on
September 9, 2026. The Google Cloud project that owns your OAuth client or
service account determines your API access level. Credentials: Local stdio mode authenticates with Application Default
Credentials (ADC) from an OAuth 2.0 client secret JSON file or a
service account in your Cloud project. Set the GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT environment variable when needed to specify your default quota or ADC
project. Remote streamable-http deployments instead require an OAuth 2.0
Web application Client ID and Client secret (see Deploy to Google Cloud
Run ). Local software (for stdio mode): Install Python 3.10 or
later , pipx , and the gcloud command-line
tool (used to generate user ADC files). Configuration Generate Application Default Credentials (ADC) using an OAuth
client from your API-enabled Google Cloud project and include the Google Ads API
scope: gcloud auth application-default login \ --scopes = https://www.googleapis.com/auth/adwords,https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform \ --client-id-file = PATH_TO_CLIENT_SECRET_JSON Replace the following: PATH_TO_CLIENT_SECRET_JSON : the path to your OAuth 2.0 client secret
JSON file. This command prints Credentials saved to file: [PATH_TO_CREDENTIALS_JSON] (such as ~/.config/gcloud/application_default_credentials.json on Linux
and macOS). To authenticate with a service account instead, skip this step
and point GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS to your service account key JSON
file, or pass --impersonate-service-account to gcloud auth
application-default login . Add the server to your host's MCP configuration file (such as ~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json , ~/.gemini/settings.json , or ~/.claude/settings.json ): { "mcpServers" : { "google-ads-mcp" : { "command" : "pipx" , "args" : [ "run" , "--spec" , "google-ads-mcp==0.0.6" , "google-ads-mcp" ], "env" : { "GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT" : "PROJECT_ID" , "GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS" : "PATH_TO_CREDENTIALS_JSON" } } } } Replace the following: PROJECT_ID : your Google Cloud project ID. PATH_TO_CREDENTIALS_JSON : the path to the ADC JSON file printed in
step 1, or to your service account key JSON file. You can omit GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS when using the default gcloud ADC
file location. To access client accounts through a manager account, set GOOGLE_ADS_LOGIN_CUSTOMER_ID (10 digits, without hyphens) in env , or
pass the login_customer_id parameter on individual tool calls. Tip: For faster startup, install the package once with pipx install
google-ads-mcp and set "command": "google-ads-mcp" (with "args": [] ). When
a new Google Ads API version such as v26.2 is released, run pipx upgrade
google-ads-mcp (or pipx run --no-cache ) to update the bundled google-ads Python client library to 35.x+ . Optional: Equip your agent with skills and the Developer Assistant The Google Ads MCP server gives your AI client live access to account reporting
data along with asset creation, video upload, and label management tools. Pair
the MCP server with the following companion tools to help your agent construct
valid Google Ads Query Language (GAQL) queries and diagnose account
performance shifts. These tools also generate client library code, such as
scripts to link created assets to campaigns or perform other unsupported
mutations: Google Ads API AI agent skills: Portable workflow modules (including google-ads-api-mcp-setup , google-ads-api-account-diagnostics , and google-ads-api-quickstart ) that help your agent use the Google Ads MCP server
with lower token overhead. Run the following command to install them
(requires Node.js ), or see the Google Ads API AI agent skills
guide for Antigravity, Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor setup: npx skills add google/skills/skills/ads Google Ads API Developer Assistant: An open-source plugin (not an officially
supported Google product) for Google Antigravity and Claude Code that
provides local Protobuf schema inspection, GAQL validation, client library
code generation, and offline conversion troubleshooting. See Choose the right Google Ads AI tool or follow the installation guide . Core capabilities The following sections describe the server's read tools, partial mutate tools,
and reference resources. Starting in v0.0.6 , tools register by default with
their category namespace prefix (such as search_search ). When upgrading
prompts or allowlists from unprefixed releases, update tool names or set an
empty prefix ( "" ) in tools_config.yaml (see Configure tool namespaces and
read-only mode ). Read tools customers_list_accessible_customers (tool list_accessible_customers ): Returns the Google Ads customer IDs directly
accessible to the authenticated user. search_search (tool search ): Builds and runs GAQL SearchStream queries from structured parameters ( customer_id , resource , and fields , plus optional conditions , orderings , limit ,
and login_customer_id ) rather than a raw GAQL string. Every query appends PARAMETERS omit_unselected_resource_names=true to fetch resource
attributes, metrics, segments, budgets, and status cleanly. metadata_get_resource_metadata (tool get_resource_metadata ):
Retrieves selectable, filterable, and sortable attributes, metrics, and
segments for a Google Ads API resource type (for example, "campaign" ). Use this
metadata to discover valid query fields—including metrics and segments added
in minor releases such as v26.2—before calling the search_search tool. Mutate tools (partial support) assets_create_asset (tool create_asset ): Creates standalone Google Ads
assets with dedicated parameters for TEXT , IMAGE , YOUTUBE_VIDEO , SITELINK , CALLOUT , and STRUCTURED_SNIPPET asset
types. Pass the extra_params dictionary for other mutable AssetService types (such as PRICE , PROMOTION , CALL , or BUSINESS_MESSAGE ), and
include root-level final_urls alongside sitelink_link_text for SITELINK assets. Local file paths ( image_asset_path ) work in local stdio mode only. For remote HTTP deployments, pass the base64-encoded image_asset_data parameter with image_asset_mime_type set to IMAGE_PNG , IMAGE_JPEG , or IMAGE_GIF (up to 20 MB). assets_upload_video_asset (tool upload_video_asset ): Uploads a
local video file ( .3gp , .avi , .flv , .mkv , .mov , .mp4 , .mpeg , .mpg , .ogg , .webm , or .wmv ) to YouTube through the
Google Ads API as a FastMCP background task in local stdio mode only. Both video_title and video_description are required parameters. The video_privacy parameter accepts UNLISTED (default) or PUBLIC (allowed
only on advertiser-owned brand channels with user OAuth). This tool returns
a Google Ads video_upload_id value (and resource name), not the 11-character
YouTube video_id . Query you_tube_video_upload with the search_search tool (filtering by you_tube_video_upload.video_upload_id ) until you_tube_video_upload.state = 'PROCESSED' . Then pass you_tube_video_upload.video_id as the youtube_video_id parameter to assets_create_asset ( asset_type="YOUTUBE_VIDEO" ). labels_manage_labels (tool manage_labels ): Creates, updates, and
removes account labels, including name, description, and hex background
color. labels_manage_label_associations (tool manage_label_associations ):
Supports CREATE and REMOVE label association operations ( UPDATE is not
supported) on CAMPAIGN , CUSTOMER , AD_GROUP , and AD_GROUP_CRITERION resources. For CUSTOMER resources, resource_id is optional and defaults
to customer_id . Pass a composite {ad_group_id}~{criterion_id} ID for AD_GROUP_CRITERION resources, and remove associations by passing either resource_id and label_id or association_resource_name . Ad-level AD_GROUP_AD labels are not supported. Note: Mutate support covers standalone asset creation, video uploads, and label
management only. The server cannot link assets to campaigns, ad groups, or asset
groups, or configure ad-level asset automation settings (such as OVERLAY_TEXT_ON_VIDEOS in v26.2). It also cannot create, modify, pause, or
enable campaigns, ad groups, ads, budgets, or bids. For unsupported mutations,
pair the server with companion code-generation tools (see Equip your agent with
skills and the Developer Assistant ). Reference resources The server exposes four read-only MCP resources that remain mounted regardless
of your tools_config.yaml settings: resource://discovery-document : JSON REST discovery overview of Google Ads API
resources, service methods, and schemas. It complements the metadata_get_resource_metadata tool, which returns selectable, filterable,
and sortable GAQL query fields. resource://metrics : HTML reference documentation for Google Ads API metrics. resource://segments : HTML reference documentation for Google Ads API
segments. resource://release-notes : HTML Google Ads API release notes covering version
changes and new features. Propose-and-confirm safety workflow Every mutate tool ( assets_create_asset , assets_upload_video_asset , labels_manage_labels , and labels_manage_label_associations ) enforces a
two-step propose-and-confirm workflow to help prevent unintended account
modifications: Propose ( validate_only=True , default): Validates inputs without
committing changes. The asset and label tools execute a live Google Ads API validate_only dry run. Because YouTubeVideoUploadService has no dry-run
mode, assets_upload_video_asset instead validates the local file and binds
its size and modification timestamp. Each tool returns human-readable change_items entries and a stateless SHA-256 checksum digest bound to
the customer_id parameter and request payload. Confirm ( validate_only=False ): After presenting the change_items list and receiving your approval, the agent calls the tool again with validate_only=False , the identical customer_id parameter and arguments,
and the checksum value from step 1. The server rejects any missing or
mismatched checksum before mutating the account. Note: The checksum value is an unkeyed SHA-256 digest of the request
parameters that works statelessly across Cloud Run instances. It prevents
accidental parameter drift or local file swaps across turns, but does not
replace access control. To hard-block mutations, disable the labels and assets namespaces in tools_config.yaml . Configure tool namespaces and read-only mode The server bundles a default tools_config.yaml file with all five tool
categories ( customers , search , metadata , labels , and assets ) enabled.
Customize tools_config.yaml to selectively enable or disable individual tools
or namespaces, change or remove namespace prefixes, or enforce a strictly
read-only deployment. Important: Whenever namespaces is non-empty, any omitted category is
disabled by default , whereas an empty namespaces: {} mapping enables all
five categories. Include every category that you want to keep enabled—a file
containing only labels: false and assets: false disables the read tools too. At startup, the server resolves tools_config.yaml in the following order: An explicit path in the GOOGLE_ADS_MCP_TOOLS_CONFIG environment variable
(recommended for local stdio hosts, whose working directory can differ
from your project folder). A tools_config.yaml file in the server's current working directory. The default tools_config.yaml file bundled with the package. If GOOGLE_ADS_MCP_TOOLS_CONFIG points to a missing file, or if any resolved
configuration file is invalid, the server raises an error at startup instead of
falling back to defaults. The following minimal tools_config.yaml file enforces a strictly read-only
deployment: namespaces : customers : true search : true metadata : true labels : false assets : false The following tools_config.yaml file customizes prefixes and filters
individual tools (for example, exposing the base64 create_asset tool on Cloud
Run while disabling the local-only upload_video_asset tool): namespaces : # Default prefix ("customers_list_accessible_customers") customers : true # Empty prefix mounts unprefixed tool names ("search") search : "" # Custom prefix ("schema_get_resource_metadata") metadata : "schema" # Enable only specific tools in a multi-tool category assets : enabled_tools : - create_asset Sample prompts to start Try the following prompts in your MCP client after connecting the server. Ask what the server can do What can the google-ads-mcp server do? Ask about customers What customers do I have access to? Ask about campaigns How many active campaigns do I have? How is my campaign performance this week? Give me a report of the top spending campaigns split by device category over the last 7 days for account 1234567890 Create assets, upload videos, and manage labels Create a callout asset with the text "Free Shipping" for account 1234567890 Upload /path/to/promo.mp4 with title "Summer Sale" and description "Summer promo video" for account 1234567890 Create a label named "Q4 Promo" with background color #34A853 and apply it to campaign 9876543210 in account 1234567890 Note: Video uploads require local stdio mode. Creating a new label and
applying it to a campaign runs two sequential propose-and-confirm cycles so the
new label_id value can be validated in the association request. Deployment on Google Cloud To share the MCP server across multiple agents or run it as a web service, host
it on Google Cloud Run or another cloud infrastructure provider instead of
running it locally. Prerequisites A Google Cloud project with the Google Ads API enabled (see Prerequisites for production access requirements). The gcloud command-line tool installed, authenticated, and
configured with an active project: gcloud config set project PROJECT_ID Replace the following: PROJECT_ID : your Google Cloud project ID. Build and push a Docker image Use Cloud Build to build and push the container image to Artifact Registry
without installing Docker locally: Create a repository in Artifact Registry: gcloud artifacts repositories create mcp-servers \ --repository-format = docker --location = us-central1 Build and submit the image from a release tag in the GitHub repository (or
from . in a local checkout if you customized Dockerfile or tools_config.yaml ): gcloud builds submit https://github.com/googleads/google-ads-mcp \ --git-source-revision = v0.0.6 \ --tag = us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/PROJECT_ID/mcp-servers/google-ads-mcp:v0.0.6 Replace the following: PROJECT_ID : your Google Cloud project ID. Rebuild and redeploy the image whenever you update google-ads-mcp or
upgrade the bundled google-ads Python client library for new Google Ads API
releases (such as v26.2). Deploy to Google Cloud Run Configure the following environment variables and secrets for your Cloud Run
service: GOOGLE_ADS_MCP_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID : The OAuth 2.0 Web application Client
ID from your API-enabled Google Cloud project for application-level OAuth
authentication. Complete the following OAuth configuration steps: Add the authorized redirect URIs for any AI clients that you plan to
connect (such as https://claude.ai/api/mcp/auth_callback , https://chatgpt.com/connector_platform_oauth_redirect , or https://antigravity.google/oauth-callback ). Add the https://www.googleapis.com/auth/adwords scope to the OAuth
consent screen under APIs & Services > OAuth consent screen > Data
Access ( Add or remove scopes ). If your OAuth consent screen publishing status is set to Testing (the default), add the Google Accounts connecting to the MCP server as Test users under APIs & Services > OAuth consent screen >
Audience ( Test users > + Add users ). GOOGLE_ADS_MCP_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET : The OAuth Client secret corresponding
to your OAuth Client ID. GOOGLE_ADS_MCP_BASE_URL : The public base URL of your MCP server (for
example, https://google-ads-mcp-xyz-uc.a.run.app ). Cloud Run assigns this
URL during initial deployment, so deploy without this variable first and
update the service afterward. GOOGLE_ADS_MCP_JWT_SIGNING_KEY (recommended for multi-instance Cloud
Run) : A persistent secret that signs FastMCP JWTs across container restarts
and horizontal scaling. GOOGLE_ADS_MCP_STORAGE_TYPE (recommended for multi-instance Cloud Run) :
Backend for OAuth client registrations and tokens. Supported values are redis , firestore , filetree (with GOOGLE_ADS_MCP_STORAGE_PATH for
non-Cloud Run VM or mounted-volume deployments), and memory . Setting a
backend-specific variable selects that backend even if GOOGLE_ADS_MCP_STORAGE_TYPE is unset. When all GOOGLE_ADS_MCP_STORAGE_* backend variables are unset, FastMCP uses its default container-local
storage; for single-instance testing with local or memory storage, pass --max-instances=1 : redis : Set GOOGLE_ADS_MCP_STORAGE_REDIS_URL (defaults to redis://localhost:6379/0 ) and install py-key-value-aio[redis] in a
custom Dockerfile . Redis expires entries automatically. firestore : Optionally set GOOGLE_ADS_MCP_STORAGE_FIRESTORE_PROJECT (defaults to the ADC project)
and GOOGLE_ADS_MCP_STORAGE_FIRESTORE_DATABASE (defaults to (default) ). Install .[firestore] in a custom Dockerfile , provision
a Firestore database, and grant the roles/datastore.user Identity and
Access Management (IAM) role to the Cloud Run service account. The
Firestore store filters expired entries on read without deleting them.
Because it stores expires_at as a string, Firestore time to live (TTL)
policies can't delete expired entries. For long-running deployments,
plan periodic cleanup or use Redis. memory : Ephemeral in-memory storage (useful only with --max-instances=1 ). GOOGLE_ADS_MCP_STORAGE_ENCRYPTION_KEY (optional) : Dedicated Fernet
encryption key (or high-entropy secret) for stored OAuth state. This setting
and GOOGLE_ADS_MCP_STORAGE_DISABLE_ENCRYPTION=true apply only when an
explicit GOOGLE_ADS_MCP_STORAGE_* backend is configured. If omitted, the
server derives an encryption key from GOOGLE_ADS_MCP_JWT_SIGNING_KEY , or
falls back to GOOGLE_ADS_MCP_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET when no JWT signing key
is set. Setting a dedicated encryption key prevents rotating that fallback
secret from invalidating stored OAuth tokens. PORT (optional) : Listening port in streamable-http mode (defaults to 8080 ; Cloud Run sets this automatically). GOOGLE_ADS_LOGIN_CUSTOMER_ID (optional) : Default 10-digit manager
customer ID (without hyphens) used when tool calls omit the login_customer_id parameter. GOOGLE_ADS_MCP_TOOLS_CONFIG (optional) : Container path to a custom tools_config.yaml file (for example, mounted from Secret Manager at /etc/mcp/tools_config.yaml to enforce read-only mode without rebuilding
the image). See Configure tool namespaces and read-only
mode . Store GOOGLE_ADS_MCP_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET and GOOGLE_ADS_MCP_JWT_SIGNING_KEY in Secret Manager and deploy the service to Google Cloud Run: gcloud run deploy google-ads-mcp \ --image = us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/PROJECT_ID/mcp-servers/google-ads-mcp:v0.0.6 \ --platform = managed \ --region = us-central1 \ --allow-unauthenticated \ --set-env-vars = "GOOGLE_ADS_MCP_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID=CLIENT_ID" \ --set-secrets = "GOOGLE_ADS_MCP_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET=MCP_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET:latest,GOOGLE_ADS_MCP_JWT_SIGNING_KEY=MCP_JWT_SIGNING_KEY:latest" After Cloud Run completes the deployment, retrieve the assigned service URL and
update the service with the GOOGLE_ADS_MCP_BASE_URL environment variable: gcloud run services update google-ads-mcp \ --region = us-central1 \ --update-env-vars = "GOOGLE_ADS_MCP_BASE_URL=https://CLOUD_RUN_SERVICE_URL" Replace the following: PROJECT_ID : your Google Cloud project ID. CLIENT_ID : your OAuth 2.0 Web application Client ID. MCP_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET : the Secret Manager secret name storing your
OAuth 2.0 Client secret. MCP_JWT_SIGNING_KEY : the Secret Manager secret name storing your JWT
signing key. CLOUD_RUN_SERVICE_URL : the hostname assigned to your Cloud Run service
(for example, google-ads-mcp-xyz-uc.a.run.app ). Authentication and security model Deploying with --allow-unauthenticated disables Cloud Run's infrastructure IAM
check ( roles/run.invoker ) so external AI clients can connect without Google
Cloud service account tokens. Authentication is delegated to the application
layer instead: When GOOGLE_ADS_MCP_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID and GOOGLE_ADS_MCP_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET are set, the server enforces Google
OAuth 2.0 on every request and returns a 401 Unauthorized HTTP status code
to unauthenticated callers. Every tool call executes under the authenticated
caller's OAuth identity. Omitting --allow-unauthenticated requires callers to pass Google Cloud
OIDC identity tokens with every request. Standard AI clients (such as Claude
and ChatGPT) use end-user OAuth rather than Google Cloud IAM tokens, so
direct connections require --allow-unauthenticated paired with
application-level OAuth. Caution: Never omit GOOGLE_ADS_MCP_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID and GOOGLE_ADS_MCP_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET when deploying with --allow-unauthenticated . Those environment variables switch the server from
local stdio mode to streamable-http transport. Without them, the server
falls back to Application Default Credentials (ADC) and exposes the container's
service account credentials to unauthenticated callers. Configure the MCP client After deployment, configure your MCP client with the Cloud Run service URL.
Because the server enforces OAuth 2.0, your client must support the MCP OAuth
flow or supply an authorized Bearer token: OAuth-enabled clients: In clients that support MCP OAuth discovery (such
as Antigravity), connecting triggers a Google sign-in prompt to grant the https://www.googleapis.com/auth/adwords scope (shown as .../auth/adwords in the Google Cloud console). Third-party AI platforms (Claude, ChatGPT): In your client's connector
settings, add a custom connector pointing to your service URL with the /mcp path (for example, https://google-ads-mcp-xyz-uc.a.run.app/mcp ).
Select OAuth 2.0 authentication with your OAuth Client ID and Client secret,
and confirm that the client's callback URI is in your OAuth client's
authorized redirect URIs. Clients without OAuth support: Clients that don't support HTTP OAuth
flows receive a 401 Unauthorized HTTP status code. For those clients, use
the local stdio configuration instead. The following example configures the gemini command-line tool in ~/.gemini/settings.json (for Google Antigravity in ~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json , replace "httpUrl" with "serverUrl" or "url" ): { "mcpServers" : { "google-ads-mcp" : { "httpUrl" : "https://CLOUD_RUN_SERVICE_URL/mcp" } } } Replace the following: CLOUD_RUN_SERVICE_URL : the hostname assigned to your Cloud Run service
(for example, google-ads-mcp-xyz-uc.a.run.app ). Page Summary outlined_flag The Google Ads API has access levels tied to the developer token and requires an application review to grant them. Start with Basic Access and apply for Standard Access as your application grows, allowing for the potential review time. The Required Minimum Functionality (RMF) only applies to developer tokens with Standard Access, so review these requirements beforehand. The Google Ads API is free to use, but non-compliance with RMF for Standard Access users may result in fees. The Google Ads API has access levels associated with the Google Cloud
project, and uses an application review process to grant various access levels.
It's important to plan and obtain the correct access levels before
productionizing your application. A common scenario is that your application development starts with Explorer
access level , but then outgrows its quota limits over time. At
that point, you should apply for Basic access level or Standard
access level . While Basic access applications are reviewed
automatically, the Standard access review process can take several business days
or sometimes weeks to complete, so request your Standard access level upgrade
well before you need the increased quota limits. Google may require that your app provide certain capabilities or features as
listed in the Required Minimum Functionality (RMF) . When using the
Google Ads API, the RMF only applies to Google Cloud projects with Standard access
level. Make sure you review these requirements in advance to avoid additional
delays around building the necessary features in your app. Pricing The Google Ads API is free to use; there are no charges for using the Google Ads API at
Explorer access, Basic access, or Standard access levels. However, if you are
subject to Required Minimum Functionality (RMF) , the API Review Team
audits your tool for compliance. If the audit results in a finding of
non-compliance, you may be required to pay non-compliance fees . Page Summary outlined_flag A developer token is required to make API calls to the Google Ads API and its access level controls the number of daily calls and environments. You need a Google Ads manager account to obtain a developer token and a Google Ads client account is the target of your API calls, identified by a 10-digit client customer ID. Making an API call requires obtaining a developer token, configuring a Google Cloud project with a service account and key for authentication, and setting up your Google Ads client account, including granting the service account access. Depending on your preference for making API calls, you can either download a client library or use HTTP clients like curl or the Google Cloud CLI. To make an API call using a client library or curl, you will need to provide your developer token, client customer ID, and the JSON key file path for your service account credentials in the configuration. This quick start guide helps you make your first API call to the Google Ads API. Key concepts Google Cloud project: A Google Cloud project forms
the basis for creating, enabling, and using all the Google services,
including managing APIs and OAuth 2.0 API credentials. You can create one
from the Google Cloud Console . API access level: The API access level of your
Google Cloud project controls the number of API calls you can make per day
and the environments to which you can make API calls. Your project's API
access level is listed on your project's Google Ads API Overview page . Google Ads manager account: A Google Ads manager
account is used to manage other Google Ads accounts, which could be a collection
of Google Ads client accounts or other Google Ads manager accounts. Google Ads client account: The Google Ads account used for running ads that you
want to target with API calls. Client customer ID: The 10-digit number that identifies a Google Ads client
account. If you copied this ID from the Google Ads UI, make sure to remove the
hyphens. OAuth 2.0: OAuth 2.0 is an industry-standard protocol
for authorization, used by all Google APIs. You need a service account and
key to generate OAuth 2.0 credentials to make API calls. Service account: A special type of Google
Account that belongs to your application rather than to an individual user.
It is used to authenticate your application to the Google Ads API. You need a
Google Cloud project to obtain a service account. Service account key: A JSON app credential file that contains the
private key for your service account. It is used to generate OAuth 2.0
credentials to authenticate a service account when making an Google Ads API API
call. You need a service account to obtain a service account key. Prerequisites To make a Google Ads API call, you should complete the following steps. Configure your Cloud project for Google Ads API access The Google Cloud project is used for managing Google APIs and OAuth 2.0 API
credentials. You can find your existing Google Cloud projects or create one by
visiting the Google Cloud console . Start by enabling the Google Ads API in your project: Enable Google Ads API Next, visit the Google Ads API Overview page . The page displays
your current API access level. If your current API access level is Test ,
then expand the Upgrade access level section. Follow the instructions to
apply for Explorer access level. Once you complete your application, Google will automatically review your
application and upgrade it to Explorer in most cases. If you weren't
granted Explorer access, don't worry; this guide will provide the appropriate
instructions when configuring your Google Ads client account . Create a service account Key Point: Note both the service account email address and the service account
key you generate in this step. You will need them when making the API calls. You need a service account and service account key to make API calls. If you are
already using another Google API and have created an OAuth 2.0 service account
and key, you can skip this step and reuse the existing credentials. How to create a
    service account and key In the Google Cloud console, go to Menu menu > IAM & Admin > Service Accounts . Go to Service
        Accounts Select your service account. Click Keys > Add key > Create new key . Select JSON , then click Create . Your new public/private key pair is generated and downloaded to your
      machine as a new file. Save the downloaded JSON file as credentials.json in your working directory. This file is
      the only copy of this key. Don't commit credentials.json to
      version control (for example, add it to your .gitignore file). Click Close . Configure your Google Ads client account Key Point: Make a note of the 10-digit Google Ads client customer ID, without the
hyphens. You'll need this ID to specify which account you're making API calls
against. Start by identifying the Google Ads account you're making API calls against. The
type of account you can make API calls to depends on the API access level of your Google Cloud project. Check your Google Ads API overview page to find out your API access level. Explorer, Basic & Standard access levels You can make calls to your Google Ads production account. However, you can
create a Google Ads test account by following the instructions on the Test
access tab if required. Test access Your Google Cloud project cannot be used to make API calls to a Google Ads
production account. You can make API calls against Google Ads test accounts
only. How to create a Google Ads
    test account The following instructions create a Google Ads test manager account and a
  Google Ads test client account underneath it. Click Create a test manager account to open the Google Ads
    account selection page. If prompted, sign in with a Google Account that
    isn't linked to your Google Ads production manager account, or click Create account to create a new Google Account. Create a test manager
    account On the account selection page, click New Google Ads
    Account (or click Create a new account if the Finish
    setting up your account? dialog appears). The account selection
    page does not display a test indicator, but opening it from Create a
    test manager account configures the signup flow to create a test
    manager account. On the Confirm your business information page, enter an Account display name , select a Primary use of the account option, select your country, time zone, and currency. Confirm the red Test account label in the upper-right corner, click Submit , and then click Explore your account to open your
    test manager dashboard. While in your Google Ads test manager account, create a Google Ads test
    client account: Click Accounts > add_circle > Create new account . Enter
    an account name, select your country, time zone, and currency, and save
    the account. Any client accounts you create from your test manager
    account are automatically test accounts. (For verification guidance,
    see View
    test accounts ). Optional: Create at least one test campaign under the
    test client account from the Google Ads page. If you skip campaign
    creation, your first API call in Make an API call succeeds but returns
    an empty response (zero campaigns). To make an API call to a Google Ads customer, you must grant access and appropriate
permissions to your service account to the Google Ads customer account. To do this,
you need administrator access to the customer account. How to grant the
      service account access to your Google Ads account Start by signing in to your Google Ads account as an administrator. Navigate to Admin > Access and security . Click the add_circle button under the Users tab. Type the service account email address into the Email input box.
    Select the appropriate account access level and click the Add account button. Note that Email access level is not supported for
    service accounts. The service account is granted access. [Optional] You cannot grant administrator access to a service
    account during initial setup. If your API calls require administrator
    access, you can upgrade the access as follows. Click the drop-down arrow next to the access level of the service
         account in the Access level column. Select Admin from the drop-down list. Download tools and client libraries Tip: Working in an AI coding agent? Install Google Ads API AI agent skills ( google-ads-api-quickstart ) for guided
setup, or connect the Google Ads MCP server for live queries. For
local schema inspection and client library code generation in Antigravity or
Claude Code, see the open-source Google Ads API Developer Assistant . You can choose to either download a client library or an HTTP client depending
on how you'd like to make API calls. Use a client library Download and install a client library of your choice. Use HTTP client (REST) curl Download and install curl , the command line tool for
transferring data through a URL. The Google Cloud Command Line Interface Follow the gcloud command-line tool installation guide to install the gcloud command-line tool. The instructions for the rest of this guide were verified to work with the
following version of the gcloud tool and might not work with previous
versions due to differences in application behavior or command-line options. :~$ gcloud version
Google Cloud SDK 492 .0.0
alpha 2024 .09.06
beta 2024 .09.06
bq 2 .1.8
bundled-python3-unix 3 .11.9
core 2024 .09.06
enterprise-certificate-proxy 0 .3.2
gcloud-crc32c 1 .0.0
gsutil 5 .30 Make an API call Key Point: The instructions refer to both a CUSTOMER_ID (the 10-digit customer
ID of the target client account in the request URL path) and a login_customer_id setting (or loginCustomerId / login-customer-id , which
is required and must be set to the 10-digit manager account ID if you
access the client account through a manager account, or omitted if you
authenticate directly to the client account). Customer IDs must not contain
hyphens (dashes) in API requests, URLs, or configurations (for example, use 1234567890 instead of 123-456-7890 to avoid an INVALID_CUSTOMER_ID error).
For more details, see the Google Ads access model and API call structure . Note: The client library instructions may refer to a particular library version.
It is meant only for illustrative purposes; you may use the latest version of
the client library unless expressly stated. Tip: Do you want to run more reporting queries? See our GAQL query builder . Learn more about reporting . Select your client of choice for instructions on how to make an API call: Java The client library artifacts are published to the Maven Central repository. To manage dependency versions and prevent conflicts, see the Google Ads API Bill of Materials (BOM) guide . If you are not using the BOM, add the client library directly to your
project using one of the following build tools: Maven : Add the following dependency to your pom.xml file: <dependency> <groupId>com.google.api-ads</groupId> <artifactId>google-ads</artifactId> <version>48.2.0</version>
</dependency> Gradle : Add the following dependency to your build.gradle file: implementation ' com . google . api - ads : google - ads : 48.2.0 ' Create an ads.properties file in your home directory ( ~/ads.properties on Linux and macOS, or %USERPROFILE%\ads.properties on Windows) with the
following content: api.googleads.serviceAccountSecretsPath=JSON_KEY_FILE_PATH
api.googleads.loginCustomerId=INSERT_LOGIN_CUSTOMER_ID_HERE Before running API requests, create a GoogleAdsClient instance. By
default, fromPropertiesFile() loads credentials from the ads.properties file located in your home directory: GoogleAdsClient googleAdsClient ; try { googleAdsClient = GoogleAdsClient . newBuilder (). fromPropertiesFile (). build (); } catch ( IOException e ) { System . err . printf ( "Failed to create GoogleAdsClient: %s%n" , e ); throw new RuntimeException ( "Initialization failed" , e ); } Next, run a campaign report using GoogleAdsService.SearchStream to stream large result sets efficiently and retrieve the campaigns in your
account: private void runExample ( GoogleAdsClient googleAdsClient , long customerId ) { try ( GoogleAdsServiceClient googleAdsServiceClient = googleAdsClient . getLatestVersion (). createGoogleAdsServiceClient ()) { String query = "SELECT campaign.id, campaign.name FROM campaign ORDER BY campaign.id" ; // Constructs the SearchGoogleAdsStreamRequest. SearchGoogleAdsStreamRequest request = SearchGoogleAdsStreamRequest . newBuilder () . setCustomerId ( Long . toString ( customerId )) . setQuery ( query ) . build (); // Creates and issues a search Google Ads stream request that will retrieve all campaigns. ServerStream<SearchGoogleAdsStreamResponse> stream = googleAdsServiceClient . searchStreamCallable (). call ( request ); // Iterates through and prints all of the results in the stream response. for ( SearchGoogleAdsStreamResponse response : stream ) { for ( GoogleAdsRow googleAdsRow : response . getResultsList ()) { System . out . printf ( "Campaign with ID %d and name '%s' was found.%n" , googleAdsRow . getCampaign (). getId (), googleAdsRow . getCampaign (). getName ()); } } } } GetCampaigns . java C# The client library packages are published to the NuGet.org repository .
Start by adding a NuGet package reference to the Google.Ads.GoogleAds package: dotnet add package Google.Ads.GoogleAds --version 27 .7.0 To make API calls, create a GoogleAdsConfig object from your configuration
settings (such as appsettings.json , environment variables, or custom
settings) and pass it to initialize a GoogleAdsClient instance: GoogleAdsConfig config = new GoogleAdsConfig () { OAuth2Mode = OAuth2Flow . SERVICE_ACCOUNT , OAuth2SecretsJsonPath = "JSON_KEY_FILE_PATH" , LoginCustomerId = "INSERT_LOGIN_CUSTOMER_ID_HERE" }; GoogleAdsClient client = new GoogleAdsClient ( config ); Next, run a campaign report using the GoogleAdsService.SearchStream method to retrieve the campaigns in your account. This guide doesn't cover
the details of reporting . public void Run ( GoogleAdsClient client , long customerId ) { // Get the GoogleAdsService. GoogleAdsServiceClient googleAdsService = client . GetService ( Services . V26 . GoogleAdsService ); // Create a query that will retrieve all campaigns. string query = @"SELECT campaign.id, campaign.name, campaign.network_settings.target_content_network FROM campaign ORDER BY campaign.id" ; try { // Issue a search request. googleAdsService . SearchStream ( customerId . ToString (), query , delegate ( SearchGoogleAdsStreamResponse resp ) { foreach ( GoogleAdsRow googleAdsRow in resp . Results ) { Console . WriteLine ( "Campaign with ID {0} and name '{1}' was found." , googleAdsRow . Campaign . Id , googleAdsRow . Campaign . Name ); } } ); } catch ( GoogleAdsException e ) { Console . WriteLine ( "Failure:" ); Console . WriteLine ( $"Message: {e.Message}" ); Console . WriteLine ( $"Failure: {e.Failure}" ); Console . WriteLine ( $"Request ID: {e.RequestId}" ); throw ; } } GetCampaigns . cs PHP The client library packages are published to the Packagist repository .
Ensure you have a compatible PHP version and Composer installed, then change
into the root directory of your project and run the following command to
install the library and its dependencies in your project's vendor/ directory: composer require googleads/google-ads-php:35.4.0 Make a copy of the google_ads_php.ini file from the GitHub repository, save it in your home directory or your
project's root directory, and modify it to include your credentials: [GOOGLE_ADS]
loginCustomerId = "INSERT_LOGIN_CUSTOMER_ID_HERE"

[OAUTH2]
jsonKeyFilePath = "JSON_KEY_FILE_PATH"
scopes = "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/adwords" Create a GoogleAdsClient instance using your google_ads_php.ini configuration file: use Google\Ads\GoogleAds\Lib\OAuth2TokenBuilder; use Google\Ads\GoogleAds\Lib\V26\GoogleAdsClientBuilder; $oauth2Credential = (new OAuth2TokenBuilder()) ->fromFile('/path/to/google_ads_php.ini') ->build(); $googleAdsClient = (new GoogleAdsClientBuilder()) ->fromFile('/path/to/google_ads_php.ini') ->withOAuth2Credential($oauth2Credential) ->build(); Note: If you omit the path in fromFile() , the client library loads google_ads_php.ini from your home directory ( ~ ) by default. In
production code, wrap client initialization and API calls in try/catch blocks to handle InvalidArgumentException and GoogleAdsException . Next, run a campaign report using the GoogleAdsService.SearchStream method to retrieve the campaigns in your account: public static function runExample(GoogleAdsClient $googleAdsClient, int $customerId) { $googleAdsServiceClient = $googleAdsClient->getGoogleAdsServiceClient(); // Creates a query that retrieves all campaigns. $query = 'SELECT campaign.id, campaign.name FROM campaign ORDER BY campaign.id'; // Issues a search stream request. /** @var GoogleAdsServerStreamDecorator $stream */ $stream = $googleAdsServiceClient->searchStream( SearchGoogleAdsStreamRequest::build($customerId, $query) ); // Iterates over all rows in all messages and prints the requested field values for // the campaign in each row. foreach ($stream->iterateAllElements() as $googleAdsRow) { /** @var GoogleAdsRow $googleAdsRow */ printf( "Campaign with ID %d and name '%s' was found.%s", $googleAdsRow->getCampaign()->getId(), $googleAdsRow->getCampaign()->getName(), PHP_EOL ); } } GetCampaigns.php Python The Google Ads API client library for Python is distributed on PyPI . Ensure you have a supported Python
version installed, then install the library using pip : python -m pip install google-ads == 35 .1.0 To authenticate your API calls, configure a google-ads.yaml file: Download a copy of the sample google-ads.yaml file from
the GitHub repository. Save the file in your home directory ( ~/google-ads.yaml ) or a custom
path. Open google-ads.yaml and update it to include your credentials: login_customer_id: INSERT_LOGIN_CUSTOMER_ID_HERE
json_key_file_path: JSON_KEY_FILE_PATH Configure logging before initializing the client so that the library
captures any initialization or configuration warnings. The following example
configures the library's logger to output INFO logs to standard output
( stdout ): import logging import sys logger = logging . getLogger ( "google.ads.googleads.client" ) logger . setLevel ( logging . INFO ) logger . addHandler ( logging . StreamHandler ( sys . stdout )) Note: You can also configure logging directly inside your google-ads.yaml configuration file. Create a GoogleAdsClient instance by calling the GoogleAdsClient.load_from_storage method and passing the path to your google-ads.yaml file: from google.ads.googleads.client import GoogleAdsClient client = GoogleAdsClient . load_from_storage ( "path/to/google-ads.yaml" ) If you omit the path argument, load_from_storage() searches for the
configuration file in your home directory ( ~/google-ads.yaml ) by default. Ensure you have a
supported Ruby version installed, and use Bundler to
install the library: Add the gem to your application's Gemfile : gem 'google-ads-googleads' , '~> 46.2.0' Install the gem by running: bundle install To configure your credentials: Copy the sample google_ads_config.rb file from the GitHub repository. Save the file in your project's root directory or your home directory
( ~ ). Open google_ads_config.rb and replace the placeholder values with your
Google Ads API credentials: Google :: Ads :: GoogleAds :: Config . new do | c | c . login_customer_id = 'INSERT_LOGIN_CUSTOMER_ID_HERE' c . keyfile = 'JSON_KEY_FILE_PATH' end Create a GoogleAdsClient instance by passing the path to your
configuration file ( google_ads_config.rb ): client = Google :: Ads :: GoogleAds :: GoogleAdsClient . new ( 'path/to/google_ads_config.rb' ) Next, run a campaign report using the GoogleAdsService.SearchStream method to retrieve the campaigns in your account: def get_campaigns ( customer_id ) # GoogleAdsClient will read a config file from # ENV['HOME']/google_ads_config.rb when called without parameters client = Google :: Ads :: GoogleAds :: GoogleAdsClient . new responses = client . service . google_ads . search_stream ( customer_id : customer_id , query : 'SELECT campaign.id, campaign.name FROM campaign ORDER BY campaign.id' , ) responses . each do | response | response . results . each do | row | puts "Campaign with ID #{ row . campaign . id } and name ' #{ row . campaign . name } ' was found." end end end get_campaigns . rb Perl The Perl client library is distributed on CPAN and requires Perl
5.28 or higher and the cpan or cpanm package manager. Clone the google-ads-perl repository in the directory of your choice: git clone https://github.com/googleads/google-ads-perl.git Change into the google-ads-perl directory and run the following
commands to install the required dependencies and build the library: cd google-ads-perl
cpan install Module::Build
perl Build.PL
perl Build installdeps
perl Build
perl Build install To configure your credentials: Copy the sample googleads.properties configuration file from the GitHub repository to your home directory
( ~/googleads.properties ): cp googleads.properties ~/googleads.properties Edit ~/googleads.properties to include your credentials: jsonKeyFilePath=JSON_KEY_FILE_PATH
loginCustomerId=INSERT_LOGIN_CUSTOMER_ID_HERE Create a Client instance by passing the path to your configured googleads.properties file (such as ~/googleads.properties ): my $api_client = Google::Ads::GoogleAds:: Client - > new ({ properties_file = > "/path/to/googleads.properties" }); Next, run a campaign report using the GoogleAdsService.SearchStream method to retrieve the campaigns in your account: sub get_campaigns { my ( $api_client , $customer_id ) = @_ ; # Create a search Google Ads stream request that will retrieve all campaigns. my $search_stream_request = Google::Ads::GoogleAds::V26::Services::GoogleAdsService:: SearchGoogleAdsStreamRequest - > new ({ customerId = > $customer_id , query = > "SELECT campaign.id, campaign.name FROM campaign ORDER BY campaign.id" }); # Get the GoogleAdsService. my $google_ads_service = $api_client - > GoogleAdsService (); my $search_stream_handler = Google::Ads::GoogleAds::Utils:: SearchStreamHandler - > new ({ service = > $google_ads_service , request = > $search_stream_request }); # Issue a search request and process the stream response to print the requested # field values for the campaign in each row. $search_stream_handler - > process_contents ( sub { my $google_ads_row = shift ; printf "Campaign with ID %d and name '%s' was found.\n" , $google_ads_row - > { campaign }{ id }, $google_ads_row - > { campaign }{ name }; }); return 1 ; } get_campaigns . pl When executed, the script streams the matching rows and prints the ID and
name of each campaign in your account. curl Start by setting the service account as the active credentials in the gcloud command-line tool. gcloud auth login --cred-file = JSON_KEY_FILE_PATH Next, fetch an OAuth 2.0 access token for the Google Ads API. gcloud auth \ print-access-token \ --scopes = 'https://www.googleapis.com/auth/adwords' Create a file named query.json containing your Google Ads Query Language
(GAQL) request: { "query" : "SELECT campaign.id, campaign.name, campaign.network_settings.target_content_network FROM campaign ORDER BY campaign.id" } Run a campaign report using the GoogleAdsService.SearchStream method to retrieve campaigns in your account: curl -i -X POST \ https://googleads.googleapis.com/v26/customers/ CUSTOMER_ID /googleAds:searchStream \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer ACCESS_TOKEN " \ -H "login-customer-id: LOGIN_CUSTOMER_ID " \ --data-binary "@query.json" Note: SearchStream returns a series of HTTP response chunks containing
batches of GoogleAdsRow JSON objects. Remove hyphens from customer IDs
(for example, use 1234567890 instead of 123-456-7890 ). If you encounter errors when making your first call, see Handle API errors for guidance on
troubleshooting.
